headings.text: We rode 70.19 km and raised $5,067 for ProBono SG's Migrant Workers Law Centre.
For ProBono SG The money went to its Migrant Workers Law Centre.
We often walk past construction sites, clean public spaces and new skyscrapers without thinking twice about the people behind them.
Most migrant workers can't afford a lawyer when this happens.

We wanted our ride to fund one specific thing. The Migrant Workers Law Centre, run by ProBono SG, gives free legal aid to migrant workers who cannot afford a lawyer, in cases like unpaid wages and wro
The MWLC is one part of a wider legal-aid network, alongside criminal defence and community law centres in Hougang and Woodlands.
ProBono SG also refers clients to social services for problems outside the law.
We started to see access to justice as something that affects people's wellbeing as well as their legal rights.
26 March 2026: our call with Tricia Teo, Manager of Development and Communications at ProBono SG.
We gave out roles at our second meeting, on 17 March. Each of us took charge of one part of the project.

findings.fix: A statement set large is about 30 words. Cut it, or set the rest as ordinary body text.
